question: E014 was surprising. Muon on the conv filters, with lookahead kept, reached 0.768 at 9 epochs, +1.3 pp over the tip and far above the predicted range. But the run took 9.18 s against the tip's 8.09 s, so the optimizer step costs about 13% more time. That much accuracy headroom is worth roughly 2 epochs, which makes H1.2 the most decision-relevant open branch. The question: how can Muon's per-step cost be cut, and how should its hyperparameters be retuned so that a Muon recipe clears 0.753 at about 6.5-7.5 epochs in less time than the tip? Specifically: (a) cheaper orthogonalization, via fewer Newton-Schulz steps (3 vs 5), tuned quintic coefficients, batching or stacking same-shape filters into one batched matmul, lower precision, or orthogonalizing less often than every step; (b) how Muon's lr, momentum, Nesterov use, and the warmup/decay schedule should change when the run is shortened to fewer epochs or steps; (c) whether Muon interacts with lookahead or EMA weight averaging, and with batch size, in short training runs.

rubric: Studies Muon or a closely related orthogonalized/spectral-norm update (Shampoo-without-accumulation, polar-decomposition-based steepest descent) and reports either its wall-clock or FLOP overhead or ways to reduce it (fewer or cheaper Newton-Schulz iterations, batching, mixed precision, lower update frequency)

Reports accuracy or loss against steps, epochs or wall-clock time in a short or compute-limited training regime, ideally on small image classifiers (CIFAR-10/100, ResNet- or airbench-style CNNs) or speedrun settings
Gives concrete hyperparameter guidance (lr, momentum, Nesterov, NS step count, schedule shape, batch size) or ablations that can be transferred to a ~7-9-epoch CIFAR-100 run on one A100
Optionally addresses how orthogonalized updates combine with weight averaging (EMA, lookahead, SWA) or label smoothing
exclude: Methods that need pretrained weights, transfer learning, distillation from a pretrained teacher, or any external data beyond the 50,000 CIFAR-100 training images
Test-time augmentation, test-set tuning, or anything that touches the test set during training or alters model state during evaluation
Techniques that require installing packages beyond PyTorch 2.4.0 / torchvision 0.19.0 (e.g. external optimizer libraries), unless the method is simple enough to reimplement in a few lines
Multi-GPU / distributed-only optimizer work (e.g. sharded Muon communication schemes) with no single-GPU compute insight
LLM-scale Muon papers whose only contribution concerns token-scale pretraining dynamics and has no transferable cost or hyperparameter findings
GPU clock or power manipulation, sleeps, or any timing tricks forbidden by RULES.md
